# Maldives TRAVEL SURVIVAL KIT **Traveler Types Covered**: Budget/Luxury/Family/Solo ## 1. SIM CARD SOLUTIONS ### Purpose: Obtain local mobile connectivity for calls, data, and internet access. Maldives has two main mobile operators: Dhiraagu and Ooredoo. Both offer tourist-friendly SIM cards at Velana International Airport (MLE) upon arrival. #### Key Information | **Aspect** | **Details to Find** | | :-------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Providers** | Dhiraagu, Ooredoo Maldives | | **Price Options** | **Dhiraagu Tourist SIM:** ~MVR 300-600+ (approx. $20-40) for various data packages (e.g., 17GB for 15 days).
**Ooredoo Tourist SIM:** Similar pricing, often with slightly different data/validity combinations (e.g., 17GB for 15 days ~MVR 450). Check for special promotions. | | **Data Allocation** | Plans range from 5GB to 100GB, valid for 7 to 30 days. High-speed 4G/5G data is standard. | | **Validity Period** | Typically 7, 15, or 30 days. Extensions may be possible but often easier to buy a new SIM for longer stays. | | **Hotspot/Tethering** | Generally allowed and works well, allowing you to share your data connection with other devices. | | **Coverage** | Excellent coverage across inhabited islands and most resorts. Strongest in Malé and major atolls. Performance on remote islands or at sea can vary. | | **Where to Buy** | **Velana International Airport (MLE):** Kiosks for both Dhiraagu and Ooredoo are located in the arrivals hall. This is the most convenient option.
**Official Shops:** Available in Malé and some larger local islands.
**Hotels/Resorts:** Some resorts may offer pre-ordered SIMs or assist with purchase, but usually at a premium. | | **Alternative: eSIM** | **Airalo / Holafly / Nomad:** Offer eSIMs for Maldives.
**Airalo (e.g., Discover+ Global eSIM):** 1GB for 7 days for $9, 3GB for 30 days for $24. Prices vary significantly based on data and validity.
**Holafly (Maldives eSIM):** Unlimited data for 5 days for $34, 15 days for $54.
eSIMs provide immediate connectivity upon arrival, no physical SIM swap needed. | #### Recommendations Framework - **Short trips (3-7 days) or resort-only stays?** → A 7-day physical SIM from the airport with a moderate data package (5-10GB) from either Dhiraagu or Ooredoo. Resorts often have Wi-Fi. - **Staying 1-2 weeks or island hopping?** → Opt for a 15-day physical SIM with higher data (15GB+) from the airport. - **Digital nomad preferences or multi-country trip?** → eSIM for convenience and flexibility, especially if you need to keep your home SIM active. - **Budget-conscious?** → Compare airport offers; Dhiraagu and Ooredoo are competitive. Avoid buying SIMs at resorts if possible. ## 2. AIRPORT TRANSFERS ### Purpose: Navigate from Velana International Airport (MLE) to Malé (Primary City Center) and other islands efficiently. #### Route: From Velana International Airport (MLE) to Malé City Center (or onward to resorts) | **Mode** | **Duration** | **Cost (MVR)** | **Booking** | **Convenience** | **Best For** | | :--------------------------- | :----------------------------------------- | :------------- | :---------------------------------------- | :-------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Public Ferry** | 10-15 minutes | 15-20 MVR | Ticket counter at ferry terminal | Good | Budget travelers, reaching Malé city center, local island transfers | | **Speedboat (Private/Shared)** | 10-15 minutes (to Malé); 30-90 min (to near atolls) | 200-1500 MVR+ | Pre-arranged with resort/guesthouse or at airport counter | Very Good | Faster transfers to nearby resorts/local islands, groups | | **Seaplane** | 20-45 minutes (to resort) | $300-600 USD+ | Pre-arranged with resort | Excellent | Luxury resorts, scenic views, direct resort access | | **Domestic Flight + Speedboat** | 1-3 hours (total) | $200-400 USD+ | Pre-arranged with resort | Good | Resorts in distant atolls | #### Detail Each Option With **Public Ferry** - **Exact boarding location:** Just outside the airport arrivals terminal, a short walk to the ferry dock. - **Frequency:** Every 10-15 minutes during the day (6 AM to midnight), less frequent late night. - **Final drop-off location:** Malé City Ferry Terminal (often called Jetty 1 or Presidents Jetty). - **How to purchase tickets:** Buy tickets from the counter at the ferry terminal. - **Operating hours:** Approximately 6:00 AM to 12:00 AM (midnight). - **Time estimates:** 10-15 minutes. **Speedboat (Shared/Private)** - **Exact boarding location:** Docks directly outside the airport arrivals terminal, look for resort/guesthouse representatives holding signs. - **Frequency:** Varies. Shared speedboats follow schedules set by resorts/guesthouses. Private speedboats can be arranged on demand. - **Final drop-off location:** Directly to your resort's jetty or a local island jetty. - **How to purchase tickets:** Most commonly pre-arranged by your resort or guesthouse. Can also be booked at counters in the airport. - **Operating hours:** Generally operates during daylight hours, but private transfers can be 24/7 if pre-arranged. - **Time estimates:** 10-15 minutes to Malé; 30-90 minutes to nearby atolls. **Seaplane** - **Exact boarding location:** After clearing customs, you will be met by resort staff who will escort you to a dedicated seaplane terminal, a short bus ride from the main airport. - **Frequency:** Seaplanes operate during daylight hours (typically 6:00 AM to 4:00 PM). Schedules are set by Trans Maldivian Airways (TMA) or Maldivian Air Taxi (MAT) based on resort bookings. - **Final drop-off location:** Directly to your resort's pontoon or a floating jetty nearby, followed by a short boat transfer. - **How to purchase tickets:** Almost always pre-arranged by your luxury resort and included in your booking package or as an add-on. - **Operating hours:** Daylight hours only. - **Time estimates:** 20-45 minutes flying time, plus transfer time to terminal and waiting. **Domestic Flight + Speedboat** - **Exact boarding location:** Check-in at the domestic terminal adjacent to the international airport. - **Frequency:** Daily flights to regional airports like Gan (Addu Atoll), Ifuru (Raa Atoll), Kadhdhoo (Laamu Atoll), Maamigili (Alif Dhaal Atoll). - **Final drop-off location:** From the regional airport, a speedboat will take you to your final resort or local island. - **How to purchase tickets:** Typically arranged by your resort. - **Operating hours:** Flights operate throughout the day. - **Time estimates:** Domestic flight (20-60 min) + speedboat (15-60 min). ## 3. CURRENCY EXCHANGE ### Purpose: Convert home currency to local currency at best rates. **Current Exchange Rate (approx. as of late 2023/early 2024)**: 1 USD = 15.40 MVR #### Best Exchange Locations | **Location** | **Why It's Best** | **Address** | **Hours** | **Rates** | **Tips** | | :----------------------- | :----------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------ | :-------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Banks in Malé** | Official rates, reliable, no hidden fees | Bank of Maldives (BML) branches, State Bank of India | Weekdays 8:30 AM - 2:00 PM | Official interbank | Best for exchanging larger amounts if you are spending time in Malé. Bring your passport. | | **Velana Intl. Airport** | Immediate access, convenient upon arrival | Arrivals Hall | 24/7 | Decent, but slightly worse than banks | Exchange a small amount for ferry/taxi to Malé or initial expenses. USD is widely accepted at resorts, so MVR might not be necessary for resort-only stays. | | **Resort Front Desks** | Convenience for resort guests | Your resort's reception desk | 24/7 | Slightly worse rates, high service fees | Only use for small amounts or emergencies. USD is the primary currency used at resorts, so exchanging to MVR might be unnecessary unless you're visiting local islands. Most transactions are charged in USD to your room and settled by card. | #### Alternative Methods | **Method** | **Pros** | **Cons** | **Best For** | | :------------------- | :--------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------- | | **ATM Withdrawal** | Mid-market rates, convenient, widespread in Malé | Bank fees (local and international), daily limits | Reliable access to cash in MVR or USD. Check if your bank reimburses ATM fees. | | **Credit Card** | Secure, no need to carry much cash, purchase tracking | Foreign transaction fees (check your card terms) | Large purchases at resorts, restaurants, dive centers. USD is often the default charge currency. | | **Bank Transfer** | Best rates if pre-arranged (for large amounts) | Time-consuming, complex for tourists | Not practical for typical tourist transactions. | #### Universal Tips - USD is widely accepted, especially at resorts. MVR is primarily needed for local islands and smaller purchases in Malé. - Avoid exchanging at small shops or unauthorized vendors. - Carry some cash in smaller USD denominations ($1, $5, $10) for tips or small purchases, even if staying at a resort. - Always check for hidden commissions or service charges before exchanging. - Confirm with your resort if MVR is needed or if USD is sufficient for all your expenses. ## 4. MUST-HAVE APPS ### Purpose: Essential applications for navigation, transport, payments, and communication. #### Category: Transportation | **App** | **Purpose** | **Key Features** | | :----------------- | :------------------------------ | :-------------------------------------------------- | | **Google Maps** | Navigation, transport routes | Real-time traffic, offline maps, ferry/bus routes | | **Local Taxi Apps** | Taxi services (limited use) | Booking taxis in Malé, upfront pricing (limited) | | **Resort/Guesthouse Apps** | Internal transport/bookings | Booking transfers, restaurant reservations (resort-specific) | #### Category: Payments & Wallet | **App** | **Purpose** | **Key Features** | | :------------------ | :--------------------- | :--------------------------------------------- | | **Bank of Maldives (BML) App** | Local banking, payments (if local account) | Transfers, bill payments (less relevant for tourists) | | **Credit Card Apps** | Monitoring expenses | Transaction tracking, fraud alerts | #### Category: Food & Delivery | **App** | **Purpose** | **Key Features** | | :-------------------- | :---------------- | :----------------------------------------- | | **BML MobilePay** | Local payments, food ordering | QR code payments, limited food delivery (Malé) | | **Local Restaurant Apps** | Food ordering | Restaurant variety, delivery (Malé only) | #### Category: Information & Entertainment | **App** | **Purpose** | **Key Features** | | :---------------- | :---------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------- | | **Viber/WhatsApp** | Communication (free calls/messages) | Essential for contacting resorts/tour operators | | **Weather App** | Local weather | Rain alerts, forecasts, marine warnings | | **Maldives Official Travel Guide** | Government travel info | Guides, landmarks, safety information (official) | | **Booking.com / Agoda** | Accommodation bookings, local info | Hotel deals, guest reviews, location details | ## 5. MUST-TRY FOODS ### Purpose: Experience authentic local cuisine and signature dishes. 🍽️ **Garudhiya (Clear Fish Broth)** – Main Course → What: A clear fish broth, typically made with tuna, served with rice, lime, and chili. It’s a staple. → Where: Local cafés and restaurants in Malé, such as "Symphony Restaurant" or smaller local eateries. → Price: 30-70 MVR (approx. $2-5 USD) → Try with: Accompanied by rice, smoked tuna (valhomas), lime, chili, and onions. 🍽️ **Mas Huni (Shredded Smoked Tuna with Coconut)** – Breakfast Special → What: A traditional Maldivian breakfast dish made from shredded smoked tuna, grated coconut, onions, and chili. → Where: Found in almost all local guesthouses and cafés. Try it at a local eatery in Malé. → Price: 25-50 MVR (approx. $1.50-3.50 USD) → Try with: Served with roshi (flatbread) and black tea. 🍽️ **Hedhikaa (Maldivian Short Eats)** – Street Snacks → What: A variety of savory and sweet deep-fried snacks, often fish-based. Examples include gulha (fish balls), masroshi (fish-filled flatbread), and bajiya (pastries). → Where: Local cafés and tea shops (Sai Hote) across Malé and local islands. → Price: 5-15 MVR per piece (approx. $0.30-1 USD) → Try with: Best enjoyed with sweet black tea (rukuri sai) during an afternoon break. 🍽️ **Bis Keemiya (Samosa-like Pastry)** – Street Snacks → What: A savory pastry similar to a samosa or spring roll, filled with tuna, cabbage, and boiled egg. → Where: Available at local cafés and short eat stalls, especially popular in Malé. → Price: 10-20 MVR (approx. $0.60-1.30 USD) → Try with: A popular snack at any time of day, pairs well with hot tea. 🍽️ **Rihaakuru (Thick Fish Paste)** – Main Course Condiment → What: A thick, dark brown fish paste made from concentrated tuna extract, often served as a condiment. Very strong, unique flavor. → Where: Used in local homes and some traditional restaurants. → Price: Small jars can be bought at local markets for 30-100 MVR. → Try with: A small amount is typically eaten with rice, roshi, or as a dip for bread. 🍽️ **Kandukukulhu (Spicy Chicken Curry)** – Main Course → What: A rich and spicy chicken curry, often cooked with coconut milk and various Maldivian spices. → Where: Local restaurants and guesthouses on inhabited islands. → Price: 80-150 MVR (approx. $5-10 USD) → Try with: Steamed rice or roshi. 🍽️ **Saagu Bondibai (Sago Pudding)** – Desserts → What: A creamy sago pudding cooked with coconut milk, cardamom, and rose water, often served with condensed milk. → Where: Local cafés and as a dessert option in guesthouses. → Price: 30-60 MVR (approx. $2-4 USD) → Try with: A light and sweet end to a meal, especially after spicy dishes. 🍽️ **Kirugarudhiya (Milk Soup)** – Beverages → What: A soothing and light soup made with fresh milk and sometimes a hint of ginger or cardamom. → Where: Local cafés. → Price: 20-40 MVR (approx. $1.30-2.60 USD) → Try with: A comforting drink, often consumed for breakfast or as a light meal. ## 6. UNIQUE & BRANDED ITEMS TO BUY ### Purpose: Purchase country-specific products worth bringing home. **Pro Tip**: While resorts have boutiques, for authentic local crafts and better prices, visit Malé's souvenir shops or local island markets. | **Item** | **Why Worth Buying** | **Where to Buy** | **Price Range (MVR)** | **Packaging Tips** | | :------------------ | :--------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Thundu Kunaa** | Traditional hand-woven mats, intricate patterns | Souvenir shops in Malé, local craft markets, Hulhumalé | 150-1000+ MVR | Can be rolled up; ensure it's protected from moisture. Larger mats might need to be checked luggage. | | **Lacquerware (Laajehun)** | Hand-crafted wooden boxes, vases, decorative items, vibrant colors | Artisan workshops in Malé and some local islands, souvenir shops | 200-2000 MVR | Fragile; wrap carefully in bubble wrap or soft clothing. Opt for smaller, more portable items if carrying in hand luggage. | | **Maldivian Sarongs (Feyli)** | Traditional patterned wraps, versatile beachwear, light and airy | Local markets, souvenir shops in Malé and Hulhumalé | 100-300 MVR | Easy to pack, lightweight. Can be folded flat in any luggage. | | **Coconut Products** | Virgin coconut oil, coconut jam (Addu Bondi), coconut shell crafts | Local markets, small shops, some guesthouses | 50-300 MVR | Oils should be in sealed, leak-proof containers and placed in checked luggage. Jams are also best in checked luggage. Coconut shell crafts are durable and easy to pack. | | **Maldivian Tea/Coffee** | Local blends, unique flavors | Supermarkets in Malé, local shops | 50-150 MVR | Pack in original sealed packaging to preserve freshness. Good for both carry-on and checked luggage. | | **Maldivian Snacks (Bondi, Gulha)** | Packaged versions of local short eats, dried fish snacks (Valhomas) | Supermarkets (STO), local mini-marts | 20-100 MVR | Ensure they are properly sealed to avoid odors and maintain freshness. Best placed in checked luggage to avoid issues with carry-on food restrictions. | | **Resort Branded Merchandise** | High-quality apparel, accessories from luxury resorts | Resort boutiques | $50-200+ USD | Usually good quality and well-packaged by the resort. Easy to pack. | | **Hand-Carved Wooden Fish/Boats** | Intricate wooden models, often depicting traditional Maldivian fishing boats (Dhoni) | Souvenir shops, craft markets | 150-1000 MVR | Wrap carefully to protect delicate parts. Larger models may require specific packing or checked luggage. | ## 7. SUPERMARKETS & CONVENIENCE STORES ### Purpose: Access everyday items, snacks, and groceries reliably. #### Major Supermarket Chains **STO Trade Centre** - **Best for**: Wide range of groceries, fresh produce, household items, electronics, and imported goods. Good for bulk buying. - **Specialty**: Largest supermarket in the Maldives, offering competitive prices and variety. - **Hours**: Sat-Thu 8:30 AM - 10:00 PM, Fri 2:00 PM - 10:00 PM (subject to prayer times). - **Locations**: Major branch at Boduthakurufaanu Magu, Malé. Also has smaller outlets. **Fantasy Supermarket** - **Best for**: Daily groceries, fresh produce, and a selection of imported snacks and beverages. - **Specialty**: Known for being well-stocked and a bit more upscale than smaller local shops. - **Hours**: Daily 8:00 AM - 11:00 PM. - **Locations**: Orchid Magu, Malé. **Agora** - **Best for**: General groceries, fresh goods, and some specialty imported items. - **Specialty**: Modern supermarket format, good for a comprehensive shopping trip. - **Hours**: Daily 8:00 AM - 11:00 PM. - **Locations**: Ameenee Magu, Malé. #### Convenience Stores **Local Mini-Marts / Kiosks** - **Best for**: Quick purchases of snacks, drinks, basic toiletries, and local essentials. - **Specialty**: Ubiquitous on local islands and throughout Malé, offering immediate access to necessities. - **Hours**: Many operate 24/7 or until very late. - **Locations**: Found on almost every street corner in Malé, Hulhumalé, and local inhabited islands. #### Pharmacy Chains **Medica Pharmacy** - **Best for**: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines, first-aid supplies, basic health and beauty products. - **Specialty**: Widely available, reliable for medical needs. - **Hours**: Generally 9:00 AM - 11:00 PM daily; some branches 24/7. - **Locations**: Multiple branches in Malé, Hulhumalé, and larger local islands. #### Department Store Supermarkets **STO People's Choice** - **Best for**: Combines a supermarket with other department store sections, offering a broader range beyond just groceries. - **Specialty**: A one-stop-shop for many daily needs. - **Hours**: Similar to STO Trade Centre. - **Locations**: Malé City. ## 8. MARKETS (Day & Night) ### Purpose: Experience local culture, find deals, and enjoy street food. The Maldives does not have the bustling night markets common in Southeast Asia. Markets are primarily for fresh produce and fish during the day. #### Day Markets | **Market Name** | **Location** | **Open Hours** | **Best For** | **What to Expect** | **Pro Tips** | | :-------------------- | :------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------- | :------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Malé Local Market** | Boduthakurufaanu Magu, near the ferry terminal, Malé | 8:00 AM - 11:00 PM daily | Fresh fruits, vegetables, local snacks, handicrafts | A vibrant indoor market with stalls selling local produce, dried fish, spices, and a few souvenir items. Less about street food, more about ingredients. | Visit in the morning for the freshest produce. Haggling is not common for food but possible for handicrafts. Good place to see local life. | | **Malé Fish Market** | Boduthakurufaanu Magu, next to the Local Market, Malé | 6:00 AM - 9:00 PM daily | Fresh fish, seafood | Watch local fishermen unload their catch. Expect a lively, authentic atmosphere, and the smell of fresh fish. | Go in the late afternoon (around 3-5 PM) to see the day's catch arrive. It's a bustling and photo-worthy experience. Be prepared for a strong fish smell. | #### Universal Day Market Tips - Carry cash (MVR) as most small vendors don't accept cards. - Visit in the morning for the best selection of produce. - Bargaining is generally not expected for food items, but you might try a little for souvenirs. - Enjoy the local atmosphere and observe daily life. - Ask before photographing people, especially vendors working. ## 9. BEST ALCOHOLIC DRINKS ### Purpose: Try region-specific beverages and understand drinking culture. Alcohol is strictly prohibited on all local (inhabited) islands in the Maldives, including Malé and Hulhumalé. It is only available at licensed resorts and liveaboards (safari boats). There are no "local beers" or "local spirits" produced in the Maldives due to religious restrictions. #### Local Beers * **None available for purchase in Maldives outside of resorts.** Resorts typically stock international beer brands (e.g., Heineken, Corona, Lion Lager, Carlsberg). #### Spirits & Liqueurs * **None available for purchase in Maldives outside of resorts.** Resorts offer a wide selection of international spirits and liqueurs (e.g., vodka, rum, gin, whiskey, cocktails). #### Wine & Rice Wine * **None available for purchase in Maldives outside of resorts.** Resorts typically have international wine lists (red, white, rosé, sparkling). #### Where to Buy | **Outlet Type** | **Best For** | **Price Level** | **Selection** | | :------------------------ | :-------------------------------------------- | :-------------- | :------------------------------------------- | | **Resort Bars/Restaurants** | All alcoholic drinks, cocktails, wines, beers | High (premium) | Excellent variety of international brands | | **Liveaboards/Safari Boats** | Beers, spirits, basic wines | Mid-High | Good selection for onboard consumption | | **Duty-free (at MLE airport)** | Bringing in (if allowed by destination) | Discount | International brands (for departure only, cannot bring into Maldives) | #### Drinking Culture Tips - **Legal drinking age**: 18. - **Where alcohol is sold**: Exclusively at resorts and licensed liveaboard vessels. It is illegal to bring alcohol into the Maldives, even from duty-free shops; it will be confiscated upon arrival at Velana International Airport (MLE). - **Social drinking etiquette**: At resorts, drinking is generally casual and accepted. On local islands, avoid any public consumption or display of alcohol. - **Tipping customs in bars**: A service charge (typically 10%) is usually added to bills at resorts. Tipping extra is optional but appreciated for excellent service. - **Peak drinking hours**: Evening at resort bars, especially around sunset and after dinner. ## 10. BEST PUBS & BARS ### Purpose: Find quality nightlife venues for evening entertainment. As alcohol is restricted to resorts and liveaboards, the "pubs and bars" scene is exclusively found within these establishments. There are no public pubs or bars on local islands like Malé or Hulhumalé. #### Rooftop Bars * **Vibe**: Upscale, romantic, offering stunning sunset views and panoramic ocean vistas. * **Location**: Various luxury resorts (e.g., W Maldives - SIP, Hard Rock Hotel Maldives - The Lagoon, Jumeirah Maldives Olhahali Island - GLOW). * **Hours**: Typically open from late afternoon (for sunset) until late evening (e.g., 5 PM - 11 PM or later). * **Specialties**: Craft cocktails, premium spirits, fine wines, often with live DJ sets or chilled lounge music. * **Pro Tips**: Dress smart-casual. Make reservations for popular spots, especially for sunset. Be prepared for high prices. #### Beach/Waterfront Bars * **Vibe**: Relaxed, barefoot luxury, perfect for enjoying cocktails by the beach or lagoon. * **Location**: Found on almost every resort island (e.g., Conrad Maldives - The Quiet Zone, Finolhu Baa Atoll - Beach Club). * **Hours**: Open throughout the day and into the evening. * **Specialties**: Tropical cocktails, fresh fruit juices, light snacks. Some have fire shows or movie nights on the beach. * **Pro Tips**: Ideal for a casual drink, often swim-up options. Great for sunset drinks. #### Nightclubs (Resort-based) * **Vibe**: High energy, dancing, often with international DJs. * **Location**: A select few larger luxury resorts might have dedicated nightclub spaces (e.g., W Maldives - 15 BELOW, Hard Rock Hotel Maldives - The Stage). * **Hours**: Late evening into the early hours (e.g., 10 PM - 2 AM). * **Specialties**: Dance music, bottle service, special events. * **Pro Tips**: Check the resort's entertainment schedule. Dress code might be smart-casual. #### Casual Resort Pubs/Lounges * **Vibe**: Laid-back, comfortable, perfect for a pre-dinner drink or a relaxed evening. * **Location**: Most resorts will have several lounge or bar options (e.g., any resort's main bar). * **Hours**: Varies, often from morning until late night. * **Specialties**: Classic cocktails, spirits, beer, sometimes light bar snacks. * **Pro Tips**: A good spot to unwind and meet other guests. --- ## BONUS SECTIONS - Local Festivals & Events - Customs & Etiquette - Health & Safety - Seasonal Tips - Money-Saving Hacks ### 11. LOCAL CUSTOMS & ETIQUETTE The Maldives is a predominantly Sunni Muslim country, and its culture is deeply influenced by Islamic traditions. Respect for local customs, especially on inhabited islands, is crucial. #### 11a. Temple & Sacred Site Dress Code The Maldives does not have temples in the same way as Buddhist countries. However, visitors should dress modestly when visiting mosques or local communities. | **Rule** | **What to Check** | **Enforcement Level** | | :---------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------- | | **Shoulders covered** | Required for both men and women when visiting mosques | Strictly enforced | | **Knees covered** | Required for both men and women when visiting mosques | Strictly enforced | | **Footwear** | Shoes removed before entry to mosques | Mandatory | | **Head covering** | Required for women when entering a mosque | Mandatory | | **Colour restrictions** | None specific | Not applicable | | **Sarong/Wrap rental** | Not commonly available; best to dress appropriately beforehand | Not common | #### 11b. The Head, Feet & Body — Cultural Hierarchy While not as strict as some Buddhist cultures regarding the head and feet, general respect for the body and personal space is observed in the Maldives. - **Head**: While not considered sacred, it is respectful to avoid touching someone's head. - **Feet**: Avoid pointing the soles of your feet at people, especially elders, or religious sites. - **Passing objects**: Generally, use your right hand when giving or receiving items, especially food or money. Using both hands is a sign of respect. #### 11c. Monk Interactions & Religious Etiquette As a Muslim country, there are no monks or associated specific interaction rules in the Maldives. | **Rule** | **Detail** | **Who It Applies To** | | :------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------- | | **Women cannot touch monks** | Not applicable | Not applicable | | **Women handing items to monks** | Not applicable | Not applicable | | **Men offering items** | Not applicable | Not applicable | | **Photography of monks** | Not applicable | Not applicable | | **Entering monastery grounds** | Not applicable | Not applicable | | **Morning alms-giving** | Not applicable | Not applicable | #### 11d. Saving Face & Conflict Resolution "Saving face" is important in Maldivian culture. Public displays of anger or aggression are considered highly inappropriate and counterproductive. - **Avoid raising your voice or showing anger in public.** Maintain a calm and respectful demeanor, even if frustrated. - **Public confrontations are to be avoided.** Address issues quietly and privately to ensure a better chance of resolution. - **Patience is highly valued.** Remain polite and persistent for more successful outcomes. #### 11e. Responsible Tourism & Child Welfare Responsible tourism practices are important in the Maldives to protect both the local community and the fragile environment. - **Do not give money or gifts to begging children.** While rare, this can incentivize children to be out of school. - **Support local businesses and communities.** Buy directly from local artisans and dine at locally owned restaurants on inhabited islands. - **Avoid orphanage tourism.** It is generally harmful and not applicable in the Maldives. - **Animal welfare is paramount.** Do not disturb marine life, touch coral, or feed wild animals unless part of a supervised, ethical activity. - **Ask before photographing people.** A smile and gesture for permission is always respectful. #### 11f. General Social Customs & Greetings Understanding basic social customs will enhance your interactions with locals. - **Greeting style**: The common greeting is "Assalaamu Alaikum" (peace be upon you). Handshakes are common between men. Women may shake hands with other women. Modest greetings between genders are respectful. - **Tipping culture**: A service charge (typically 10%) is usually added to resort bills. Tipping beyond this is optional but appreciated for exceptional service (e.g., MVR 50-100 for a guide or boat crew, $5-10 USD for resort staff). - **Dress outside temples**: On local islands, modesty is expected. Women should cover shoulders and knees. Men should wear t-shirts and shorts/trousers. Swimwear is only appropriate on resort islands or designated tourist beaches. - **Photography restrictions**: Avoid photographing military installations or government buildings. Always ask permission before taking close-up photos of individuals. - **Public displays of affection**: Avoid public displays of affection (kissing, hugging) on local islands. - **Bargaining norms**: Bargaining is not common in supermarkets or fixed-price shops. It might be possible at small souvenir stalls, but usually for a small discount. - **Dining etiquette**: Food is often eaten with the right hand or with a spoon and fork. It's common for dishes to be shared. ### 12. SAFETY & PRACTICAL INFORMATION Safety in the Maldives is generally high, especially on resort islands. However, visitors should be aware of specific considerations when on local islands or exploring the marine environment. #### 12a. Vaccinations & Preventative Health Consult a travel medicine specialist 6-8 weeks before your trip to ensure you are up-to-date on all recommended vaccinations. | **Vaccine / Medication** | **Priority Level** | **Notes** | | :--------------------------------- | :------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Hepatitis A** | Strongly recommended | Transmitted through contaminated food/water – essential for any developing country | | **Hepatitis B** | Recommended | Especially for longer stays or those with potential exposure | | **Typhoid** | Recommended | High risk in areas with poor sanitation and street food consumption | | **Tetanus / Diphtheria (Td/Tdap)** | Recommended | Ensure booster is current (within 10 years) | | **Japanese Encephalitis** | Destination-specific | Not generally required for typical tourist travel to resorts or Malé | | **Rabies pre-exposure** | Destination-specific | Only recommended for adventurous travelers with potential animal contact, less common | | **Malaria prophylaxis** | Generally NOT needed | The Maldives was certified malaria-free in 2015. | | **Cholera** | Destination-specific | Only for high-risk flood/disaster zones, not typical for tourists | #### 12b. Mosquito-Borne Illness & Insect Protection Mosquitoes are present in the Maldives and can transmit diseases. Protection is advisable, especially on local islands and in vegetated areas of resorts. | **Disease** | **Mosquito Type** | **Peak Risk** | **Prevention** | | :--------------- | :----------------------- | :-------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------- | | **Dengue Fever** | Aedes (daytime biting) | Rainy season (May-Nov) | DEET repellent, covered clothing, mosquito nets (if needed) | | **Malaria** | Anopheles (night biting) | No risk | Not applicable (Maldives is malaria-free) | | **Zika Virus** | Aedes | Rainy season (May-Nov) | DEET, covered clothing (important for pregnant travelers) | | **Chikungunya** | Aedes | Rainy season (May-Nov) | DEET, covered clothing | #### 12c. Personal Safety & Crime Awareness The Maldives is generally very safe for tourists, particularly on resort islands. Violent crime is rare. However, petty crime and specific scams can occur in Malé and on some local islands. ISSUE: **Petty Theft / Pickpocketing** WHERE IT HAPPENS: Crowded areas in Malé, such as markets, ferry terminals, and busy streets. HOW IT HAPPENS: Opportunistic theft from open bags, pockets, or unattended belongings. HOW TO AVOID IT: Keep valuables secure and out of sight. Use a cross-body bag. Do not flash large amounts of cash or expensive electronics. Be aware of your surroundings in crowded areas. WHAT TO DO IF IT HAPPENS: Report to the local police station (Malé City Police) immediately and inform your guesthouse/resort. Contact your travel insurance company. ISSUE: **Bag-snatching from Motorbikes** WHERE IT HAPPENS: More common in Malé and Hulhumalé, especially on busy roads. HOW IT HAPPENS: Thieves on motorbikes may snatch bags, phones, or cameras from pedestrians. HOW TO AVOID IT: Walk on the side of the pavement away from traffic. Keep bags strapped across your body and worn on the side away from the road. Do not openly hold phones or cameras on busy streets. WHAT TO DO IF IT HAPPENS: Do not resist forcefully, as this can lead to injury. Report to the police and your embassy. ISSUE: **Swimming and Ocean Safety** WHERE IT HAPPENS: Unsupervised beaches, strong currents, reefs. HOW IT HAPPENS: Undercurrents can be strong, especially around channels between islands. Injuries from coral can occur. HOW TO AVOID IT: Always swim in designated areas, especially around resort islands. Pay attention to warning flags. Do not swim alone. Be mindful of tides and currents. Wear reef shoes to protect against sharp coral or sea urchins. If you are not a strong swimmer, use a life vest, especially during water activities. WHAT TO DO IF IT HAPPENS: Seek immediate medical attention for injuries. Inform your resort or tour operator if you encounter dangerous conditions. ISSUE: **Unlicensed Tour Operators / Excursions** WHERE IT HAPPENS: Can be encountered in Malé or on some local islands. HOW IT HAPPENS: Offers for tours, snorkeling trips, or other activities at suspiciously low prices may be from unlicensed operators who cut corners on safety or quality. HOW TO AVOID IT: Book tours and excursions through your resort, guesthouse, or reputable, well-reviewed tour companies. Verify licenses and insurance. Ask about safety equipment and protocols. WHAT TO DO IF IT HAPPENS: If a service is unsatisfactory or unsafe, report it to your guesthouse/resort and consider informing the Maldives Tourism Promotion Board if severe. ISSUE: **Scams (Rare but possible in Malé)** WHERE IT HAPPENS: Tourist areas in Malé. HOW IT HAPPENS: Can include overcharging by taxi drivers (less common with regulated systems), or attempts to sell counterfeit goods. HOW TO AVOID IT: Agree on taxi fares before starting the journey. Be cautious of unsolicited offers for tours or goods. Purchase goods from reputable shops. WHAT TO DO IF IT HAPPENS: Politely decline or walk away. If you feel threatened, seek assistance from a local police officer. #### 12e. Emergency Contacts & Practical Infrastructure Knowing emergency contacts is essential for any travel. SEASONAL CONSIDERATIONS The Maldives experiences a tropical monsoon climate with two main seasons: - **Dry Season (Northeast Monsoon):** December to April. Characterized by less rain, lower humidity, and calm seas. This is peak tourist season. - **Wet Season (Southwest Monsoon):** May to November. Characterized by more rain (often in short, heavy bursts), higher humidity, and choppier seas. Occasional storms are possible. **What to pack accordingly:** - **Dry Season:** Lightweight, breathable clothing. Sunscreen, hats, sunglasses are essential. Swimwear. - **Wet Season:** Similar lightweight clothing, but also a light rain jacket or umbrella. Still pack sun protection for sunny spells. Seas can be rougher, so consider if prone to seasickness. ### 14. GENERAL TIPS - **Power sockets and voltage:** Type G (three-pin rectangular, UK standard). Voltage is 230V at 50Hz. Bring a universal adapter. - **Wi-Fi:** Resorts offer good Wi-Fi. On local islands, guesthouses have Wi-Fi, but a local SIM provides better personal connectivity. - **Dress modestly on local islands:** Respect local customs by covering shoulders and knees. Swimwear is for resort beaches only. - **Tipping:** A 10% service charge is often included at resorts. Additional tipping for excellent service is appreciated. - **Currency:** USD is widely accepted at resorts. MVR is needed for local islands. ATMs are available in Malé. - **Eco-tourism:** Support sustainable practices. Do not touch coral or marine life. Dispose of trash properly. - **Sun protection:** The Maldivian sun is intense. Use high SPF sunscreen, wear hats, and seek shade during peak hours. - **Footwear:** Flip-flops or sandals are suitable for almost all occasions. - **Free activities:** Many resorts offer complimentary non-motorized water sports like kayaking or paddleboarding. Snorkeling directly from the beach is often free.
